title: Russian attack on eastern Ukrainian city of Kramatorsk kills at least 33
summary: A Russian bomb attack on the eastern Ukrainian city of Kramatorsk killed at least 33 people, authorities said Thursday, describing it as a targeted strike on ‌civilians in the key stronghold sought…

image.caption: A burning bus is shown following a Russian airstrike in the city of Kramatorsk, in Ukraine's Donetsk region, on Thursday. (Press service of the National Police of Ukraine/Reuters)

blocks.text: A Russian bomb attack on the eastern Ukrainian city of Kramatorsk killed at least 33 people, authorities said Thursday, describing it as a targeted strike on ‌civilians in the key stronghold sought by Moscow.
Ukrainian president says attack hit a bus stop

Another 18 people were wounded in one of the largest single attacks of this year, which took place on a street where two city ​buses were operating at the time, police said. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described it as a bus stop.
Images posted by police showed bodies strewn across a street littered with ​debris, as well as a charred shell of what appeared to ⁠be a bus.

"For ⁠them [the Russians], a bus with passengers ‌is an attractive target, precisely because one strike can kill as many people as possible," regional governor Vadym Filashkin said on the Telegram app.
Firefighters work at the site of a Russian airstrike, where a bus was hit in Kramatorsk on Thursday. (Press service of the State Emergency Service of Ukraine in Donetsk region/Reuters)
There was no immediate comment from Moscow on the attack.
Russia denies ⁠targeting civilians, though it has regularly pounded Ukrainian cities, towns and other targets during its full-scale invasion that began in February 2022.
Moscow's forces have stepped ‌up drone and guided-bomb strikes on Kramatorsk and other cities in Ukraine's "fortress belt," local officials say, the backbone of its defences in the Donetsk region.

Russia has demanded that Ukraine cede the rest of the region still ​under its control before it stops fighting, which Kyiv refuses to do. The pace of Moscow's battlefield ⁠gains in the region has significantly slowed this year.

blocks.text: Filashkin said he had ordered ⁠city authorities in Kramatorsk and Sloviansk, another key fortress-belt city, to halt ⁠public transport, ⁠saying "we have no right to ​risk" citizens' lives.
Thursday's attack came a day after dozens were killed in a massive ​Russian air attack ⁠across Ukraine, primarily targeting the country's power grid.

Separately on Thursday, three people were killed and 14 wounded in morning drone strikes on the capital of Kyiv, said Mayor Vitali Klitschko. Russian forces have unleashed frequent waves of attacks on Kyiv amid a shortage of ⁠Ukrainian air defences.
